newsitem.title: USA: US Sen Lott-gross tax cut could be under $135 bln.
newsitem.headline: US Sen Lott-gross tax cut could be under $135 bln.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Friday he viewed the tax figures presented in the budget deal as meaning a maximum of $135 billion gross tax cuts over five years and a "minimum" of $85 billion net cuts.

He acknowledged that the Republican chairmen of the congressional tax-writing committees have said it might be difficult to get the full $50 billion in revenue increase included in last week's budget deal.
"It will not be more than $135 billion gross, it may be less," the Mississippi Republican said of the tax cuts over five years.
Asked if the net tax figure might slip below the target of $85 billion over five years, Lott replied: "We need to have a minimum -- minimum -- of a net of $85 billion in tax cuts."

Lott said the consumer price index would not be touched legislatively, but rather there would be an assumption of a 0.3 percentage point adjustment by the Bureau of Labor Statistics when it updates the formulation for the inflation indicator.
"We're not going to breath on it," Lott said.
